summary: Vehicle geometry proximity/contact test. Transforms a probe point a2 into the vehicle-local frame via sub_4EA930, then rotates it (together with a reference vector a3) by the 3x3 matrix stored at this+0x34B0..0x34D0. Builds a contact-normal candidate by cross product and a relative position by vector add. Iterates up to four vehicle corners (positions at this+0x3594 with 62-float stride, squared-distance threshold at v18[31], contact pointer at this+0x828 with active byte at this+0x868); on a hit computes an anisotropic contact response scaled by the per-corner scalar this[62*i+3436] that adjusts the relative position. Writes *a4 = signed projection of the position onto the rotated normal and *a5 = AnisoVectorTripleProduct result. If a6 is non-null, corrects the contact point and writes the response through F_33MatrixVectorMultiply into a6, returning a6; otherwise returns null. On the per-frame collision path.

operations.description: sub_4EA930(a2, this + 3381, &v38) transforms the probe point a2 into the vehicle-local frame relative to the origin vector this+3381, returning a 3-component result (v8, v9, v31).
Rotate the local vector (v8, v9, v31) by the 3x3 matrix at this+0x34B0..0x34D0 (columns this[3372..3380]) into the corner-space position (v35, v36, v37).
Rotate the second input vector a3 by the same matrix into the normal-space components (v26, v27, v28).
F_3DCrossProduct(&v38) computes the cross product of the local vector into the contact-normal candidate (v32, v33, v34).
Vec3Add(v41) sums vectors into the relative position (v29, v30, v31) used by the corner loop and the final projection.

Iterate up to four vehicle corners: position pointer v18 starts at this + 3429 (offset 0x3594) with a 62-float stride, contact pointer v17 starts at this + 522 (offset 0x828) with a 74-float stride; stop after 4 iterations.

Per corner, compute the squared distance from (v35, v36, v37) to the corner position; break when it is below the corner threshold squared v18[31]^2 (offset 0x3610) AND the corner contact pointer at v17 is non-null AND the active byte at v17 + 64 (offset 0x868) is set.

On a corner hit, build the anisotropic response: v21 = -(v34 * this[v20 + 3436]) and v22 = v33 * this[v20 + 3436] using the per-corner scalar at index v20 + 3436, then v23 = v28 * v22 + v27 * v21 (plus v26 scaled by the near-zero global constant flt_59E440, folded to 0.0 in the raw text), and adjust the relative position (v29, v30, v31) by the scaled normal components.
Write the signed projection *a4 = v31 * v28 + v30 * v27 + v29 * v26, the dot of the relative position with the rotated normal (contact depth along the normal).
Compute *a5 = AnisoVectorTripleProduct(this, &v35, &v26) — the anisotropic triple-product contact response.
If a6 is non-null, correct the contact point by subtracting the depth-scaled normal, then write the response through F_33MatrixVectorMultiply(&v38, a6) and return the result pointer a6.
Return a6 when a response vector was requested, otherwise return null.
